title: Treat customer-facing chatbot output as an accountable company communication
description: Illustrative reference decision modelled on the reasoning in Moffatt v. Air Canada (2024 BCCRT 149), where a tribunal rejected the argument that a company is not responsible for its own chatbot's statements. Not a documented decision of any specific organization.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty.

Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources). Normalized a duplicated relationship-reason phrasing ("...via this design pattern." -> "...via this single, primary design pattern.") to one canonical wording.

decision_statement: Any customer-facing AI chatbot's substantive statements (pricing, policy, eligibility) must be treated as binding company communications subject to the same accuracy review, correction, and escalation process as a human agent's statements — not as a disclaimed third party's output.
decision_context: Motivated by Moffatt v. Air Canada, in which the airline unsuccessfully argued its chatbot was 'a separate legal entity' responsible for its own errors.
governing_body: Illustrative example — Customer Experience Technology Governance Board
alternatives_considered: Disclaim chatbot statements as non-binding and rely on terms-of-service fine print.
Route all policy-sensitive queries to a human agent instead of the chatbot.

citations.title: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149
citations.publisher: Civil Resolution Tribunal of British Columbia

relationships.reason: This decision is modelled directly on the tribunal's reasoning in this incident.
The decision is put into practice via this single, primary design pattern.
Holding chatbot output to the same accuracy bar as human agents satisfies the transparency/information obligation this control describes.
Compliance must be demonstrated by a record of chatbot response accuracy review.
Boards adopting this decision should be asking about liability exposure for chatbot errors.
